title: Field-free and Sub-ns Magnetization Reversal in Synthetic Anti-ferromagnets using Sequential Spin-Orbit Torque and Spin-Transfer Torque Pulses
abstract: Single free-layer Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (MTJs) with a perpendicular easy axis driven by spin currents have demonstrated fast, deterministic switching, non-volatility, and low-power memory capabilities when integrated with modern nanoelectronic devices. In this article, we numerically investigate sub-ns and field-free switching characteristics of a p-MTJ with a Synthetic Antiferromagnet (SAF) based free layer structure using sequential sub-ns current pulses of Spin Orbit Torque (SOT) and Spin Transfer Torque (STT). While the SOT pulse applied to one layer decreases the transition time by bringing the coupled layers into an in-plane configuration, the subsequent STT pulse on the system determines the switching direction. Various pulse protocols have been investigated for both SOT and STT current amplitude and pulse widths, while also considering the effect of the Reference Layer (RL). While significant regions of deterministic switching events are observed, limitations in SOT, STT parameters are further investigated in presence of thermal fluctuations.
summary: This work numerically investigates magnetization reversal in SAF-MTJs using combined SOT and STT pulses. By applying a sequential SOT-STT protocol, the authors demonstrate achieving field-free, sub-nanosecond switching. This research is crucial for developing next-generation, high-speed, low-power magnetic memory devices.
main_problem: The research investigates achieving fast, field-free magnetization reversal in Synthetic Antiferromagnets (SAFs) integrated into Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (MTJs). The goal is to utilize sequential spin-orbit torque (SOT) and spin-transfer torque (STT) pulses to achieve sub-nanosecond switching.
main_result: The sequential SOT-STT pulse protocol successfully drives the magnetization reversal, achieving deterministic switching regions and demonstrating the feasibility of energy-efficient, high-speed operation.
method: The study employs a micromagnetic framework to numerically solve the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation, incorporating SOT and STT torque terms.
model_or_system: The physical system is a p-MTJ with a SAF-based free layer. The model incorporates magneto-static, anisotropic, and inter-layer exchange coupling terms, allowing for the simulation of magnetization dynamics in various coupled states (P and AP).
key_observables: Switching times ($\zeta_t$), threshold current densities ($J_{STT,0}$), and phase maps showing deterministic switching regions.
important_parameters: Pulse amplitudes ($J_{	ext{SOT}}, J_{	ext{STT}}$), pulse widths ($	au_{	ext{SOT}}, 	au_{	ext{STT}}$), and the pulse gap ($W_{	au}$).
main_assumptions: The effect of STT torque on FL-1 is assumed to be small and is neglected in some simulations; the pulse-gap ($W_{	au}$) is often taken to be zero.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic, the applied SOT/STT pulse profiles, the four possible magnetization states, and time evolution plots of magnetization components ($m_z$) under different pulse sequences.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical model (LLG equation with SOT/STT), then comparing pure STT and pure SOT switching mechanisms, and finally detailing the optimized, successive SOT-STT pulse protocol to achieve the fastest and most deterministic switching.
why_interesting: While the core physics is spintronics, the detailed, non-linear dynamics governed by coupled differential equations (LLG) and the analysis of switching thresholds via phase diagrams connect to the study of non-equilibrium dynamics and energy landscapes, which are relevant to open quantum systems.
